name: Sunflower
model: written by hand (Claude) from the Urdu KB

aspects.overview:
Sunflower is an important oilseed crop; Pakistan imports most of its edible oil, so more oilseed area and yield are needed. Seed has about 40 to 45 percent high-quality oil with vitamins A, B, E and K, good for heart health; the oil cake is good animal feed. The crop takes about 100 to 125 days and needs little water, so it fits easily into crop rotations, and it is a good choice when rabi crops couldn't be sown on time. Heavy loam is best; don't grow it on waterlogged or saline land. Punjab average yield was about 22 to 26 maunds per acre (2019-20 to 2023-24), on roughly 48,000 to 90,000 acres.
Rotations: cotton – spring sunflower – cotton; rice – spring sunflower – rice; peas – spring sunflower – rice or autumn maize; potato – spring sunflower – fodder; sugarcane – spring sunflower – autumn maize; spring sunflower – kharif fodder – wheat; wheat – autumn sunflower – wheat.
aspects.varieties:
Recommended hybrids: Hysun-33, T-40318 and Agora-4 (ICI Pakistan); Gulbahar-436 and S-278 (Green Gold); Augsun-5270 and Raina (Sethi Seeds); US-666 and US-444 (Umer Seeds); NK Armoni and NKS-278 (Syngenta Pakistan). Oilseeds Research Institute Faisalabad varieties: Orisun-648, -516, -675, -701, -641 and -651, and PARC's Parsun-3 (seed of these will be available in coming years). Buy seed of recommended varieties only from authorised dealers of registered companies.
Seed rate: 2 kg per acre, germination above 90 percent, 22,000 to 23,000 plants per acre; don't keep more plants than recommended (more disease, lower yield).
Seed treatment before sowing: azoxystrobin + clothianidin at 2 to 3 g per kg of seed, or tebuconazole 1.5 ml in 30 ml water per kg of seed. Seed that is already treated doesn't need it again.
aspects.sowing:
Sowing time in Punjab:
South Punjab (Dera Ghazi Khan, Rajanpur, Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan, Multan, Vehari, Bahawalnagar, Muzaffargarh, Layyah, Lodhran, Bhakkar, Khanewal): spring 1 December to 31 January; autumn 25 July to 10 August.
Central Punjab (Mianwali, Sargodha, Khushab, Jhang, Sahiwal, Okara, Pakpattan, Faisalabad, Toba Tek Singh, Chiniot, Lahore, Mandi Bahauddin, Hafizabad, Kasur, Sialkot, Gujranwala, Sheikhupura, Nankana Sahib): spring 1 to 31 January; autumn 25 July to 10 August.
North Punjab (Narowal, Attock, Rawalpindi, Gujrat, Jhelum, Chakwal): spring 1 January to 15 February; autumn 25 July to 10 August.
Avoid the frost (raya) days. Late sowing lowers both yield and oil. In rain-fed areas sowing depends on rainfall.
Land: deep plough (chisel plough), especially after rice where a hard layer forms; level with a laser land leveller.
Methods: ridges 2.5 feet apart running east–west made with a ridger; irrigate the furrows and dibble one seed every 9 inches on the south side, a little above the moisture line. Or beds about 3 feet apart (north–south) with seed on both sides. Or drill in rows 2.5 feet apart at workable moisture (wattar), seed no deeper than 2 inches. With a drill or planter, thin at the four-leaf stage to 9 inches between plants. Earth up the plants when about one foot tall.
aspects.fertilizer:
Weak soil needs 60 kg nitrogen, 40 kg phosphorus and 25 kg potash per acre. Any one of four options:
1) Sowing: 2 bags Nitrophos + 1 bag SOP; 1st irrigation: 2 bags Nitrophos; 2nd irrigation: 0.75 bag CAN; at bud stage: 0.5 bag CAN.
2) Sowing: 1.75 bags DAP + 1 bag SOP; 1st irrigation: 0.5 bag urea; 2nd: 1 bag urea; bud stage: 0.5 bag urea.
3) Sowing: 1.75 bags DAP + 1 bag SOP; 1st irrigation: 1 bag CAN; 2nd: 1.5 bags CAN; bud stage: 1 bag CAN.
4) Sowing: 4.5 bags SSP (18%) + 0.5 bag urea + 1 bag SOP; 1st irrigation: 0.5 bag urea; 2nd: 1 bag urea; bud stage: 0.5 bag urea.
Medium (average) soil needs 48 kg nitrogen, 34 kg phosphorus and 25 kg potash per acre:
1) Sowing: 1.75 bags Nitrophos + 1 bag SOP; 1st irrigation: 1.5 bags Nitrophos; 2nd: 0.5 bag CAN; bud stage: 0.5 bag CAN.
2) Sowing: 1.5 bags DAP + 1 bag SOP; then 0.5 bag urea at the 1st irrigation, 0.5 at the 2nd and 0.5 at bud stage.
3) Sowing: 1.5 bags DAP + 1 bag SOP; 1st irrigation: 1 bag CAN; 2nd: 1 bag CAN; bud stage: 0.75 bag CAN.
4) Sowing: 3.75 bags SSP (18%) + 0.5 bag urea + 1 bag SOP; then 0.5 bag urea at the 1st irrigation, 2nd irrigation and bud stage.
In short: medium soil 1.5 bags DAP, 1.5 bags urea and 1 bag SOP per acre; weak soil 1.75 bags DAP, 2 bags urea and 1 bag SOP.
Also: sulphur 5 kg per acre (or half a bag of gypsum); zinc about 6 kg per acre; if boron is short, borax 11% at 3 kg or boric acid 17% at 2.5 kg per acre at sowing. These recommendations come from the Soil Fertility Research Institute, Punjab.
Mix crop residues back into the soil (rotavator or disc harrow) or compost them: this returns nutrients, improves fertility and cuts fertilizer need.
aspects.irrigation: A drilled crop usually needs 4 to 5 irrigations, more in hot dry weather and fewer in cool humid weather or after winter rains. Schedule: 1st irrigation 20 days after germination (spring crop) or 15 days (autumn crop); 2nd 20 days later (spring) or 12 to 15 days later (autumn); 3rd at flowering; 4th at seed formation; 5th at the milky stage. On ridges or beds irrigate as the crop needs. In heat, don't let the spring crop run short of water at flowering, or pollination fails and part of the head stays empty. During seed formation in hot weather give light irrigations at intervals and never let it go dry; drought raises disease, stunts plants and cuts seed. Drain extra water after heavy rain.
aspects.pests_diseases:
Pests: termites, grasshopper, whitefly, jassid, aphid, cutworm, mites, armyworm and American bollworm.
Termites: ant-like, pale yellow; attack roots and hollow the stem so the plant dries. Apply chlorpyrifos 40 EC at 1.5 to 2 litres per acre or fipronil 5% SC at 1 litre per acre with irrigation before land preparation.
Grasshopper: spray lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5 EC or bifenthrin 10% EC at 250 to 300 ml per acre.
Jassid (green, about 3 mm; worst in March–April; leaf edges curl down, leaves yellow then dry): spray nitenpyram 25 SP 100 g or dinotefuran 20 at 100 g per acre.
Whitefly (spreads viruses, worse in hot dry weather), aphid, cutworm (cuts seedlings at night), mites (worse when the crop is short of water) and armyworm/American bollworm (attack leaves and the closed flower head from late March): spray a recommended insecticide; the exact product names are not clear in my notes, so check with the local agriculture extension office.
Friendly insects: ladybird beetle, chrysoperla, pirate bug, syrphid/hover flies, spiders and assassin bugs eat pests. Don't spray during pollination, to protect them and the pollinators.
Diseases: stem (charcoal) rot, head rot, seed mould, downy mildew and powdery mildew.
Charcoal stem rot: black lower stem, plants break or wilt; spread by seed and soil, worse with heat and drought. Treat seed (azoxystrobin + clothianidin 2 to 3 g per kg); spray difenoconazole 1 ml, tebuconazole 1.5 g, or azoxystrobin + difenoconazole 2 ml per litre; pull out diseased plants; avoid drought; at least a two-year rotation; don't overcrowd; early sowing has less of it.
Head rot: brown spots on the back of the head that grow and turn black; the head rots and falls; spreads near maturity via birds and insects. Control birds and insects, remove diseased plants, treat seed with difenoconazole 1.25 ml per kg; if severe spray mancozeb 2 g per litre.
Downy mildew: spots on leaves with dark growth underneath, thick yellow midrib, leaves curl and dry; worse in humid weather at flowering. Rotate, don't over-water, and spray difenoconazole 1 ml, mancozeb 2 g, or cymoxanil + mancozeb per litre.
Powdery mildew: white powder on leaves that turn yellow, brown and dry. Rotate, avoid drought, spray difenoconazole 1 ml per litre.
Seed mould: loose seed with mould on it; dry seed well.
Parrots: damage at germination, seed formation and maturity, mostly morning and evening. Use shiny ribbons or flags, drums, a watch platform (machan) or firecrackers, and don't sow near trees.
aspects.weeds: The first eight weeks matter most; after that the crop shades out weeds. Within 12 to 24 hours of sowing, in moist soil, spray pendimethalin 800 ml per acre in 120 litres of water. Hoe a drilled crop at least once before the first irrigation; hoeing kills weeds, breaks crust and lets air and water in. Earthing up at about one foot also kills weeds and stops lodging in wind and at maturity. Don't hoe right after spraying.
aspects.harvesting:
Harvest when the back of the head turns from green to golden, the yellow petals dry, the green bracts turn brown and the seed inside is hard. Cut the heads (by hand or trimmer), spread them in the sun for 2 to 3 days, then thresh with a thresher or a modified combine harvester. Before storing or selling, clean and dry the seed to no more than 8 percent moisture and 2 percent trash; the grain should crack when bitten. Damp seed gets mould. Sunflower oil cake is good animal feed.
Home refining of oil: extract oil with a kohlu or expeller; heat 5 kg of crude oil to about 85 °C without boiling, stir in 150 g of finely ground fuller's earth for 5 minutes, take off the fire and filter warm through a cone-shaped filter cloth bag.
aspects.machinery: Chisel plough for deep ploughing (especially after rice), laser land leveller, ridger or bed maker, drill or planter, trimmer for cutting heads, thresher or modified combine harvester for threshing; rotavator or disc harrow to mix residues into the soil.
aspects.other: Earth up at one foot height. Don't keep more plants than recommended. Sunflower fits many rotations and is a good option when rabi crops are sown late.

timing.sowing: spring: 1 December to 15 February depending on area (south Punjab 1 December to 31 January; central 1 to 31 January; north 1 January to 15 February); autumn: 25 July to 10 August
timing.harvesting: about 100 to 125 days after sowing, when the back of the head turns golden
